title: Enterprise onboarding — comprehensive support, escalation, integration & QBR playbook
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the enterprise onboarding process for Redwood Inference customers: pre-sale readiness, kickoff, technical integration, pilot-to-production cutover, ongoing health checks, Quarterly Business Review (QBR) cadence, and the escalation matrix used by Support, Customer Success, and Engineering. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, SRE on-call, and account-facing Product/Engineering leads.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers to under 6 weeks for a standard integration.
- Ensure consistent handoff between SEs and CSMs.
- Provide a clear, tested escalation path for Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
- Standardize QBR agenda and health-check metrics.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted Redwood API and Redwood Dedicated customers.
- Private/on-prem customers should follow the same high-level phases; see the Private Deployment Reference (link in related pages) for network/KMS specifics.

1) Roles & ownership
Use the table below to identify primary and secondary owners during onboarding and escalation.

| Role | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Responsibilities |
|------|---------------|----------------|------------------|
| Customer Success Manager (CSM) | customer-success | go-to-market | Relationship, QBRs, business context, success plan |
| Solutions Engineer (SE) | eng-developer-experience | customer-success | Technical kickoff, integration plan, telemetry, runbook handoff |
| Support Engineer | customer-success | eng-sre | First-line triage, ticketing, runbook execution |
| SRE / On-call | eng-sre | eng-platform | Incident response for platform/runtime outages |
| Account Engineering / Escalation | eng-serving-runtime | product | Deep technical ownership for model/runtime issues |

2) High-level onboarding phases
Each phase includes deliverables, owners, and typical duration.

Phase A — Pre-kickoff (1-5 days)
- Deliverables: NDA & contract signed, account created, initial entitlement and scopes (models, regions, traffic limits).
- Actions: CSM/SE collect access requirements, compliance needs, contact matrix, and expected SLA.

Phase B — Kickoff (1 day)
- Attendees: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, network/security, product manager (optional).
- Agenda: goals & success criteria, timeline, data flow diagram, security requirements, API key management, rate limits, and pilot plan.
- Deliverable: Onboarding Project Plan (shared Confluence page + ticket in JIRA).

Phase C — Integration (1-3 weeks)
- SE leads integration checklist: network & firewall rules, API auth, SDK onboarding, model selection, test prompt sets, telemetry hooks.
- Deliverable: Integration report with test results, baseline latency/cost metrics, and monitoring dashboard links.

Phase D — Pilot (1-4 weeks)
- Run representative workload against Redwood endpoints. Measure latency P50/P95, token cost, error rates, and output quality.
- Execute regression guardrails: annotated prompt set and acceptance criteria.
- Rollout policy: start with small percentage traffic (10-25%), monitor 48-72 hours, then increase.

Phase E — Production cutover & 30/60/90 day health checks
- Cutover checklist: API keys swap plan, rollback steps, alert thresholds verification, canary traffic pattern.
- Deliverable: Production Handover and 30/60/90 Day Success Plan.

3) Integration checklist (technical)
Use this checklist during the Integration phase; SEs must mark complete and attach artifacts to the onboarding ticket.

Network & Security
- Whitelist IP ranges (for Dedicated/Private provide BG info).
- Configure egress rules for VPCs and outbound TLS.
- Verify customer KMS/HSM integration (if required).

Authentication & Rate Limits
- Provision API keys with appropriate scopes.
- Agree rate limits and quotas; document burst/baseline expectations.

SDK & API Validation
- Run SDK quickstart and confirm sample requests succeed.
- Validate streaming responses and function/tool-calling behaviors (if used).

Model & Cost Baseline
- Confirm selected model variants and quantization profiles.
- Establish cost baseline: tokens/unit, average prompt+completion size.

Telemetry & Observability
- Ensure request tracing headers are forwarded.
- Configure logs: request/response sampling policy, error exports.
- Create per-route dashboards (latency, errors, token usage).

Failover & Rollback
- Document fallback model variants and region failover policy.
- Prepare rollback playbook with explicit toggles and owner.

4) Escalation playbook (triage matrix)
Severity definitions and initial response SLA (internal):
- Sev1 (Critical): Production outage impacting >50% of customer traffic or data loss. Response: 15 minutes. Escalate to SRE and Account Engineering.
- Sev2 (High): Degraded performance (P95 latency > 2x target) or high error rate (>5% for 30+ minutes). Response: 30 minutes. Escalate to Support Engineer + SE.
- Sev3 (Medium): Functional but non-critical bugs, intermittent errors. Response: 4 hours. Owned by Support Engineer.
- Sev4 (Low): Questions, feature requests, or minor documentation issues. Response: 2 business days.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage: Support Engineer reproduces issue and collects request IDs, traces, and relevant logs.
2. Mitigation: Apply short-term mitigation (rate-limits, routing to fallback model, temporary scaling) where possible.
3. Notify: CSM notifies customer for Sev1/2 within the SLA window; share interim RCA timeline.
4. Escalate: If mitigation not available in 30 minutes for Sev1, route to on-call SRE and Account Engineering.
5. Postmortem: For Sev1 incidents, Engineering writes a detailed postmortem (blameless) with action items and owners within 7 days.

Contacts & Pager matrix (example)
- Support queue: support@redwood.ai (monitored 24x7)
- SRE Pager: +1-555-0100 (on-call roster)
- Account Engineering: account-eng@redwood.ai (escalation alias)
- CSM Pager: CSM on-call rotation (internal calendar link)

5) Known issues and workarounds (top recurring items)
Issue: Intermittent 502 on streaming responses
- Symptom: Streaming connection drops mid-response, client sees 502.
- Root cause (common): Upstream proxy timeouts or transient GPU OOM.
- Workaround: Enable client-side retry with resume token; fall back to non-streaming endpoint if retries fail. Increase proxy timeout for streaming endpoints.

Issue: Increased P95 latency after model update
- Symptom: Sudden jump in P95 by 30-80ms after deploying a new model binary.
- Root cause: Kernel selection path or quantization mismatch on some instance types.
- Workaround: Roll back to previous model variant; trigger targeted canary on smaller traffic slice and run kernel compatibility tests.

Issue: Authentication failures after key rotation
- Symptom: 401s / invalid token errors during scheduled key rotations.
- Root cause: Clients still use cached keys or edge caches not invalidated.
- Workaround: Confirm token TTL, invalidate edge caches, coordinate rotation window with customer and support.

6) Support process & ticketing standards
Ticket creation & labeling
- All inbound customer issues must have: customer_id, environment (dev/staging/prod), model_id/route, request_ids, and severity label.
- Labels: customer:<customer_shortname>, sev:X, area:integration|runtime|auth|billing.

Triage runbook (initial 30 minutes)
1. Verify reproducibility and scope.
2. Collect request IDs, logs, and relevant dashboards.
3. Determine if mitigation is possible; apply if safe.
4. Escalate based on severity.

Communications
- For Sev1, open a dedicated Slack channel (customer-<shortname>-incident) and document updates every 15 minutes until resolved.
- For Sev2, cadence is 30-60 minutes depending on impact.

SLA commitments and exceptions
- Support will aim to meet response SLAs defined above. Contractual SLAs for Dedicated/Enterprise customers may have different targets—always defer to contract and attach the SLA ID in the ticket.

7) Health checks and QBRs
Standard health-check cadence and metrics:
- 30/60/90 day checks: adoption metrics, error rates, latent trends, cost vs forecast, and model quality regressions.
- Metrics to monitor: Monthly active routes, P50/P95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), token usage, cost per 1k tokens, regression alerts triggered.

QBR agenda (60 minutes)
1. Introductions & business outcomes (5m)
2. Adoption & usage trends (10m)
3. Reliability & incidents since last QBR (10m)
4. Cost breakdown and optimization opportunities (10m)
5. Product roadmap & upcoming platform changes (10m)
6. Action items & success plan (10m)
7. Open discussion & next steps (5m)

QBR deliverables
- Dashboard snapshot (PDF link), action item list with owners and due dates, updated success plan.

8) Templates & runbooks (appendix)
Onboarding checklist (example items):
- Access: API key provisioned, IP whitelisting complete, TLS validated.
- Telemetry: tracing headers passed, dashboards created.
- Testing: sample prompt set executed with acceptance criteria met.
- Security: data residency and retention confirmed, KMS integrated (if required).

Sev1 quick mitigation checklist:
1. Collect request IDs + trace IDs.
2. Put temporary rate-limit if noisy traffic.
3. Switch traffic to fallback model/region.
4. Notify customer and escalate to SRE.

Appendix: Useful links (internal)
- On-call roster and escalation calendar
- Dedicated deployment reference architecture
- Observability dashboards templates

If you are a CSM/SE reading this: attach completed checklists and integration report to the onboarding ticket and schedule the 30-day health check during the pilot phase. For any ambiguity in runbooks or missing artifacts, escalate to the Account Engineering alias.
